name: Plasma; spray dried; at processing plant
description: This unit process is a gate-to-gate dataset of  spray drying of 9.6574 lb of plasma in the US.

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Represents production at the national level.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The process technology assumes ~10% solids and same energy required to spray dry milk.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Includes only energy inputs for spray drying.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Includes only energy inputs for spray drying.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: This inventory data is incomplete, but because the inclusion rate in pig diets is small we did not focus to compile full life cycle invenotry of spray dried plasma. Thus, we focused on estimating energy requirements to produce to spray dried plasma, which in our assumption are equal to energy requirements of drying milk. Input data was adjusted for solid content.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Data is not of high quality due to small amount of spray dried plasma used in pig diets. One data sample (drying of milk) was used.
processDocumentation.dataCollectionDescription: Data was collected during an ongoing project from 2013 through 2015.

sources.name: Development of Life Cycle Inventory data for U.S. Swine Production Scenarios

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
